title: 7-round AES-192: MixColumns-equality differential

target.description: Standard AES-192 under the paper's round numbering: initial whitening k0, rounds1 onward; last MixColumns omitted for 7-round recovery variants. Guess k7 bytes0,1,4,7,10,11,13,14 and w6 bytes1,4, then recover8 whitening bytes:144 bits of named subkey material. These are selected round-key values, not an independently priced complete192-bit master key.

setting.key_relation: Two unknown AES-192 master keys K and K'=K XOR Delta, where Delta[0]=Delta[8]=a!=0 and the other22 bytes are0. Initial whitening is k0; round subkeys are k1,... .
setting.key_population: General unknown key pair with attacker-chosen nonzero a; b,c are actual key-dependent S-box output differences, not independently chosen subkeys.
setting.plaintext_model: Two pools of approximately2^36 inputs, total2^37 CP. For a wrong outer guess, the failed-equality filter retains fraction1-2^-8; the budget uses2^71 processed pairs.
assumptions: The source models pair filters and incorrect whitening-key eliminations probabilistically; those independence assumptions have not been proved for every AES key.
Named subkey bits may be dependent. No complete192-bit master-key recovery budget is supplied.
The source uses64 memory accesses per encryption equivalent; this is an accounting convention, not an independent implementation measurement.
b and c are computed from the guessed bytes. Data2^37 is the source's rounded acquisition estimate;2^71 is its elimination-pair budget.

data.note: Total plaintext-block encryption queries across exactly2 related keys, not a per-key budget.

memory.note: Author-reported memory; do not reinterpret the exponent as128-bit blocks.

preprocessing.note: The shared Section4 precomputation is about2^62 encryptions; no complete additional setup total for this extension is separately supplied.

success.description: The144-bit output consists of80 outer guessed subkey bits and64 whitening bits. The source probability-one MixColumns equality preserves the correct tuple; it is not a rare right-pair occurrence. With the source assigned mean mprime=2^71, the wrong-whitening survival model and all2^80 outer guesses yield E_model W <= 2^144 exp(-128). The source-rounded2^37 query and2^145 processing budgets are unchanged. This is the paper mean-count model, not a lower-tail guarantee that a random fixed plaintext budget always supplies2^71 useful pairs. Derived first-moment lower bound within the source random-filter model for a unique correct complete stated partial-subkey output. It is not an author-printed aggregate percentage, an experimental rate, or a proved actual-AES success probability; no full master-key recovery is asserted. Correct-tuple retention plus P_model(W>=1)<=E_model W supplies the implication without independence between different wrong tuples or auxiliary trials. The repeated-filter uniformity/independence assumptions are inherited from the source; the source also substitutes mean retained-pair counts for random counts, which is not justified as an actual-cipher upper bound by this audit.

components.description: Section6: under the stipulated first-round state difference and actual Table2 related-key schedule, the two designated bytes after MixColumns are equal with probability1. This is the AES-side identity, not recovery success.
Section6 source model: a fraction1-2^-8 of pairs violates the equality under a wrong terminal hypothesis and can be used to eliminate whitening guesses. This is a pair-selection fraction.

Section6 source uniform-elimination model for ONE fixed wrong64-bit whitening guess after2^71 useful pairs. The source2^64 multiplier describes expected wrong survivors under a terminal hypothesis, not a probability that all144-bit output material is uniquely recovered.

review.scope: Verified exact-edition source extraction, full stored-output and same-budget loop mapping, right-candidate retention and first-moment arithmetic. Independent source-first and endpoint review. This verifies the conditional model inference, not actual-cipher random-filter assumptions, mean-count substitution, attack reproduction or a new full-paper audit.

limitations: Independent local checks cover the AES key schedule and deterministic components. Full cryptanalytic searches, resource calibration and success rates have not been reproduced.
